  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to
Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City Council
Meeting of October 12, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. (Or 1:00 P.M. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic
means, as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, City Clerk staff will check and print emails prior to arriving in the Council
  Chambers. In the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received will be made part of the official
  public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  October 12, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California, held a regular meeting on
  Tuesday, October 12, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
  Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ Parking
  Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a
  quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/
  Parking Authority Chairman /Joint Powers Authority Chairman
  Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/ Parking Authority Members/ Joint Powers
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority
  officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking Authority,
  and Joint Powers Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/
  Housing Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority
  Chairman inquired if there were any persons who wished to address the City
  Council/Successor Agency/ Housing Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint Power
  Authority on any item on the Agendas, other than the public hearing.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown), commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. DR-
  1, Resolution adopting gross annual income guidelines for the City’s Utility Users Tax
  Refund Program for low-income seniors, and the Refuse Collection and Water Services
  Fee Discount Program for seniors and disabled citizens, and 2, Approval of the Minutes
  of the Meetings held on July 20, 2021, July 27, 2021, July 30, 2021 (Special), August 3,
  2021, August 5, 2021 (Special), and August 10, 2021.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/ Housing Authority dated
  October 8, 2021, in the amount of $1,702,996.45 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/
  Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify
  upon said registers that said demands are approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson,  Padilla,  Morales,  Faulk,  and  Mayor/Successor  Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.
   October 12, 2021

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 22-01 INTRODUCED –
  AMENDING CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  MODIFY REGULATIONS FOR SMOKE SHOPS, CITYWIDE. The City Clerk
  announced the next schedule matter was a public hearing to consider the introduction of
  an Ordinance approving Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) to amend
  Chapter 12 (Planning and Zoning) of the Inglewood Municipal Code to modify
  Regulations for Smoke Shops, Citywide, that notice had been given in the time, form, and
  manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no communications were
  received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, introduced speaker Christopher Jackson, Sr., Economic and
  Community Development Department Director.

  Christopher Jackson, Sr., Economic and Community Development Department Director
  presented the staff report dated October 12, 2021.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on the Public Hearing.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed public comment at the hour of 2:17 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby Affirm Categorical Exemption (EA-CE-2021-020).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Mayor Butts that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 22-01 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  TO  APPROVE  ZONING  CODE
  AMENDMENT 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) TO AMEND CHAPTER 12
  (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  MODIFY REGULATIONS FOR SMOKE SHOPS

  was introduced by Council Member Padilla.

126  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on July 20, 2021, July
  27, 2021, July 30, 2021 (Special), August 3, 2021, August 5, 2021 (Special), and August
  10, 2021, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the City Attorney’s Office recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Amended Claim Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1) Tadele Hadush for alleged personal injury; pavement condition on April 6, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does herby reject amended claim listed as A-1. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   October 12, 2021

183  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – EMCOR SERVICES/MESA ENERGY SYSTEM
  (EMCOR). Staff report dated October 12, 2021, was presented recommending
  authorization to pay Invoice Number 910009072 submitted on September 14, 2021, by
  EMCOR Services/Mesa Energy System (EMCOR), for emergency repairs to the Senior
  Center Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) building air condition system.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby authorized payment in the amount of $45,207.85. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  RESOLUTION NO. 22-04 ADOPTED – ADOPTING GROSS ANNUAL INCOME
  GUIDELINES FOR THE CITY’S UTILITY USERS TAX REFUND PROGRAM
  FOR LOW INCOME SENIORS AND THE REFUSE COLLECTION AND
  WATER SERVICES FEE DISCOUNT PROGRAM FOR SENIORS AND
  DISABLED CITIZENS. Staff report dated October 12, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution adopting gross annual income guidelines for the
  City’s Utility Tax (UUT) Refund Program for low-income seniors, and the Refuse
  Collection and Water Services Fee Discount Program for senior and disabled citizens.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 22-04 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING GROSS ANNUAL
  INCOME GUIDELINES FOR THE CITY’S UTILITY USERS TAX
  REFUND PROGRAM FOR LOW INCOME SENIORS, AND THE
  REFUSE COLLECTION AND WATER SERVICES FEE DISCOUNT
  PROGRAM FOR SENIORS DISABLED CITIZENS

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  PUBLIC HEARING SET – RECEIVE PUBLIC INPUT, REGARDING THE
  REDRAWING OF CITY COUNCIL DISTRICT BOUNDARIES IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE FAIR MAPS ACT. Staff report dated October 12,
  2021, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to receive input from the
  public, regarding the redrawing of City Council district boundaries, in accordance with
  the Fair Maps Act.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for October 26, 2021, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

114  APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY COMMISSION RATIFIED –
  DISTRICT 3. Upon recommendation of Council Member Morales, Mayor Butts
  appointed Alex Monge to the Housing Advisory Commission representing Councilmanic
  District 3 for the term ending November 2024. The appointment was carried and ratified
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Brown Act Violations, specifically regarding the
  time limits allowed to speak on Agenda Items. She also questioned when were the Police
  Oversight Commission meetings held, and the vandalism of the Memorial Statue located
  in front of City Hall. Finally, she requested a response to her emails and phone calls.

  3
 October 12, 2021

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Item Nos. PH-1, Ordinance approving
  Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001) to amend Chapter 12 (Planning
  and Zoning) of the Inglewood Municipal Code to modify Regulations for Smoke Shops,
  Citywide, and SPH-1, Setting a public hearing to receive input from the public, regarding
  the redrawing of City Council district boundaries, in accordance with the Fair Maps Act.
  He stated that he would like to receive the newsletter from District 4 Council Member.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Measures H & I, and requested more
  information.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on the parking permit program and requested
  quantitative data of the parking complaints received by residents. He also asked for the
  opt-in option for the parking permit program for Parking Zone 11, consistent with
  Parking Zones in District 2.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:51 p.m.

  Approved this 26th day of October, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
